neighbours.label: ' on' or ' upon' after set or determined (set on doing, set upon, determined upon, set on the beach)
fire: He was young, ambitious and set on winning the seat.
The two men were set upon by a gang near the docks.
The king had determined upon a war with his neighbors.
Set on a quiet hill, the inn has fine views.
She is set on studying medicine in Boston.
The travelers were set upon by wolves at night.
The novel is set on a small island near Greece.
They were bent and set on revenge for years.
quiet: He was young, ambitious and keen on sailing in the bay.
The two men were looked on by a gang near the docks.
The king had agreed on a truce with his neighbors.
Built on a quiet hill, the inn has fine views.
She is working on a thesis in Boston.
The travelers were spied on by wolves at night.
The novel is sold on a small island near Greece.
They were carried on a raft for days.

notes: Card: ' on' x26, ' upon' x6, nearly always after set. Probes: 'set on uncovering' 1.010, 'Set on the famous beach' 0.606, 'set upon' 0.579, 'determined upon' 0.301; other verbs 0.014. Near misses keep ' on' after other verbs, so the token alone can't pass.
